Orgs Overview

Contents

·

    Introduction

    Org is a document interchange format. Yay, the world needs another!

    That said, org-mode is a lifestyle built around using org files to help organize your life in a variety of ways. Org Mode has strong roots in many common methodologies like GTD, while at the same time using org mode files for almost everything in your life.

    OrgS is a server that manages a collection of org files. It offers:

    • A flexible extensible module based architecture.

    • An exporter framework that can convert an org file to a variety of outputs

      • gantt - Export an org file as a gantt chart

    • mermaid - Export a diagram in an org file using mermaid js

      • mindmap - Generate a mind map from an org file

    • html - Convert an org file to an html file

      • revealjs - Convert an org file to a revealjs presentation
      • impressjs - Convert an org file to an impressjs presentation
      • latex - Export an org file to a latex file (pdf)
      • dndsheet - Render a D&D character sheet as html
      • dndlatex - Render a D&D character sheet as latex
      • dndpdf - Render a D&D character sheet as a pdf

    • An importer framework for syncing periodically with 3rd party services

      • git
      • google calendar
      • ics files
      • jira
      • todoist
    • Quick capture methods - capture input in a variety of ways
    • Refiling and archiving capabilities

    • Generators

      • daypage - Create and jump to a daily log file
      • dnd - Build Dungeons & Dragons characters and render their sheets
    • Fast table evaluation
    • A flexible query language
    • Clocking in and out
    • A flexible notification system.

    A command line interface for interacting with your org files from the command line

    Uses

    OrgS is intended to be like the Language Server Protocol of org files. It is intended to support:

    • org protocol synchronization
    • web portal access to your org files
    • rich robust editor integrations for your org files.
    • a notification mechanism that works across platforms
    • command line access to your org files.

    Your editor, your browser and your terminal on the same notes

    Every client talks to the one server, so they share one clock, one inbox, one set of saved queries and one focus timer. Clock in from your editor and the clock is running in worg and at the command line; tick a task off on your phone and your editor's agenda shows it done.

    • VS Code: vscode-org-everywhere (Org Everywhere). Org mode editing (folding, TODO keywords, tables, links, dates) works on its own. With an orgs server it adds the agenda and the clock in the side bar, clocking in on the heading under the cursor, a focus timer in the status bar that clocks in through the server, capture through the server's templates, refile and archive, table formulas, running code and exporting. Every worg view (kanban, gantt, clock report, search…) opens as an editor panel, and a heading picked in one opens in the editor.
    • Sublime Text: Org Everywhere. A fork of OrgExtended where editing stays in the plugin and everything that spans files (the agenda, clocking, capture, refile and archive, ids and backlinks, search, exporting) is done by orgs. Org: Set Up a Local orgs Server downloads orgs and runs it on your folder of notes; Org: orgs Open Web UI opens worg on one of its views.
    • worg, the web front end the server hands out at /: every view, in any browser, including a phone's. See worg, in pictures.
    • The orgs command line: the same views at a prompt, for scripts, git hooks and ssh. See The command line, in pictures.

    The stories show them working together over a whole week: an engineer at the command line and in worg, and a writer working on a book.

    Plans

    • Mu4E style imap email synchronization and exposure of your emails as part of your org repository.

    The command line, in pictures

    What this is

    A tour of the orgs command line: one picture per command worth seeing, and the line that draws it. Every command talks to a running orgs serve (or runs one in-process for itself with -local), so they all see the same notes, and anything changed in one shows up in the others and in worg.

    The pictures are of a small demo notebook kept in docs/screenshots/demo; tools/screenshots takes them again (see Taking the pictures again).

    Every command also takes -json, -format, -dry-run and -no-color, so what is drawn here for a person can be read by a program instead.

    The day at a glance: orgs dash

    One screen that answers "what does today want from me": the agenda, the clock, the focus timer, the habits, the inbox and your watches, read together. It only reads; each card names the command that acts on it. orgs dash -w keeps it on screen, redrawn as things change, and orgs dash -json gives every card as data.

    A card whose part of the server is missing or broken says so in one dim line, and the others still draw.

    The morning standup: orgs standup

    What you did since the last working day (Friday, on a Monday), what is on today and what is in the way, written in Slack's markup so it can be pasted straight into a channel. -copy puts it on the clipboard as well, -md writes GitHub Markdown instead, -since mon starts from a day of your choosing and -n caps each section (the rest are counted).

    Every part is read by the view it comes from (the agenda, the clock table, the weekly review's waiting list, the dependency check), so a standup never says something the agenda would contradict.

    The week in review: orgs recap

    A week or a month on one page: what was finished, where the time went, how the habits held up, words written and what is still blocked. Like orgs standup it is Slack's markup unless you ask for -md.

    orgs recap                        # the last seven days
orgs recap -last -week            # last week, Monday to Sunday
orgs recap -month                 # this month so far
orgs recap -from 2026-10-01 -to 2026-10-15
orgs recap -block 2026-Q3 -md     # a clock table range, as Markdown

    The agenda: orgs agenda

    Three months of calendar, today's entries, and the week underneath. , and . step a day, n comes back to today, t changes the keyword of the entry under the cursor, m opens the month.

    Planning the day: orgs plan

    The day as hours: what is booked, what is free, and the tasks waiting for a slot, most urgent first. It is the agenda's day planner in worg, at a prompt.

    One screen for everything: orgs tui

    A query's results in a list, with the heading's body beside it. : changes the query, / filters what is there, t changes a keyword, enter opens the heading in your editor.

    Asking questions: orgs search

    The same query language worg's Search tab uses. Plain words match headlines; an expression can ask anything the database knows.

    orgs search 'IsTask() && HasTags("work")'
orgs search 'DeadlineWithin("7d")' -json | jq '.[].Headline'

    Boards: orgs kanban

    worg's kanban boards, the same boards, editable from the terminal. H and L move a card between columns (which changes its keyword), J and K reorder it, t picks a keyword, c clocks in.

    Schedules: orgs gantt

    A saved query drawn as a gantt chart, the same plan worg draws: EFFORT sizes a bar, AFTER and ORDERED chain them, weekends are skipped, and -crit marks the critical path.

    Column view: orgs cols

    org's column view of a file, from its #+COLUMNS: line. Parents total the columns that ask for it (%EFFORT{:}), enter edits a value in place, s sorts within each parent.

    Habits: orgs habits

    Every habit's last month at a glance: █ kept, ░ missed, · not due. orgs habits done <name> ticks one off.

    Tables: orgs tables

    Every org table in your notes, in a picker with the table drawn beside it. ctrl-e runs its #+TBLFM formulas.

    The weekly review: orgs review

    Everything that wants a decision: projects with nothing to do next, deadlines nobody scheduled, things waiting on somebody else, time booked against open tasks. orgs review -fix walks them one at a time.

    Flashcards: orgs drill

    Spaced repetition over your notes, org-drill style: the same cards, the same algorithms, the same DRILL_* properties. See Flashcards for how to write cards.

    What is in there: orgs stats

    Finding your way: orgs help

    Everything the command line can do is described by the binary itself, so the help always matches the version you are running. It needs no server.

    You type You get
    orgs help every command, grouped by what it is for, in the order worth reading
    orgs help standup one command: what it does, its flags, examples and what the guides say
    orgs help stand no such command, so the names it might have meant (standup)
    orgs help -all every command with every flag, one after another, for searching
    orgs help -json the command list as a table (name, group, usage), for a script
    orgs help -man search a command's man page (roff); with no command, orgs(1)
    orgs help -man-dir DIR orgs.1 and an orgs-<command>.1 for every command, written into DIR
    orgs completion zsh tab completion for your shell

    A command's page reads top to bottom like this:

    Some ways to use it:

    # Which command has a flag for this?
orgs help -all | grep -B20 -- '-since' | grep '^orgs '

# Read a long page in a pager (search has the whole query language)
orgs help search | less -R

# Real man pages: write them once, then `man orgs-search`
orgs help -man-dir ~/.local/share/man/man1

# The list for a launcher or a wrapper script
orgs help -json | jq -r '.[] | "\(.Name)\t\(.Usage)"'

    Commands you add yourself show up too: every filter in your yaml is a command, listed under its own group (or "Other"). orgs p is the same list as a fuzzy picker, together with your saved queries and aliases.

    Taking the pictures again

    The pictures are taken by a script, against a demo server with its own notes, so they can be taken again whenever a command changes:

    cd tools/screenshots
npm install
node capture.mjs                  # every picture
node capture.mjs cli-kanban       # just the ones named
node capture.mjs serve            # just the demo server, to look around

    The demo notes are in docs/screenshots/demo. Their dates are written as {{D+3}} and filled in when the script runs, so the agenda is always about today. Terminal pictures run each command in a pseudo terminal and draw the screen with xterm.js; worg pictures drive Chrome with puppeteer.

    An annotated picture (cli-dash) is a terminal picture with numbered badges and a legend. Its notes find their parts by text on the screen (a card's top edge, or a line), so the badges follow the layout, and a renamed card fails the shot instead of putting a badge in the wrong place. These shots are taken last, because they set the demo up first (a pomodoro, a ticked habit, a watch that fires) and the other pictures shouldn't show that.

    The stories' pictures live in tools/screenshots/stories/, one module a story. Each brings its own notebook (docs/screenshots/<story>/) and runs on a server of its own after the pictures above, so nothing one story sets up shows in another. node capture.mjs -story writer takes just one story's.

    worg, in pictures

    What worg is

    worg is the web front end built into the server: orgs serve hands it out at /, so any browser that can reach the server (a phone included) has it. It works on the same notes as the command line and the editor plugins; a change made in one is in the others a second later.

    It has a light and a dark look, picked with the moon in the top corner.

    The pictures here are of the demo notebook in docs/screenshots/demo, taken by tools/screenshots (see Taking the pictures again in the command line tour).

    Agenda

    The day as a planner: habits at the top, the hours of the day with what is booked into them, and the tasks still to place down the side, most urgent first. Drag a task onto an hour to schedule it. Week and Month show the wider view; the calendars mark days with something on them.

    Search

    The query language in a form: an expression, a regular expression over the text, and filters by keyword, tag and property. Rows can be edited where they are; Inspect opens a heading's dates, drawers and body beside the table.

    Files

    Every org file, read rendered or as org, and edited in place. Drawers fold, links follow, and the Links panel shows what points at the file and what it points at.

    Pictures a file links to are drawn under their links in the Org view and in the editor, as Emacs does with org-display-inline-images. The picture button on the toolbar (Images on the editor's status line) shows or hides them all; an eye at the end of a link's line, there when the pointer is, shows or hides that one. Click a picture to see it full size.

    Kanban

    Boards built from a saved query, one column per keyword (or per tag or property value). Dragging a card to another column changes the heading in its file.

    Gantt Chart

    A saved query as a schedule: EFFORT sizes the bars, AFTER and ORDERED chain them, today is the red line. Bars can be dragged to reschedule, coloured by state, person or any property, and split into lanes.

    Column View

    org's column view of a file, from its #+COLUMNS: line, with totals on each parent. Any cell can be edited in place.

    Tables

    Every org table, opened as a spreadsheet. Formulas (#+TBLFM) are shown and recalculated, cells are edited in place, and a selection can be charted. See Tables for the formula language.

    Mind Map

    A saved query drawn as a map, coloured by branch, keyword or tag, and exported as an image.

    Contacts

    Headings with a RECORD property, as an address book: upcoming birthdays at the top, a vCard import, and each contact's fields and notes beside the list. See Records.

    Flashcards

    Spaced repetition over your notes, org-drill compatible. A deck is a query; clozes hide part of a line until you ask for the answer. See Flashcards.

    Weekly Review

    GTD's weekly review as steps: empty the inbox one item at a time (refile, schedule, tag, archive, done), then the projects with no next action, what is waiting on others, last week's time and the stale scheduled items.

    Code

    Every source block in your notes, by language, with syntax colouring; a block can be run and its results written back under it.

    API

    • GET /newtemplate/list — New-File Templates, With Where Each Comes From The templates /newtemplates names, each with whether it is built in, whether this server has its own copy, and which one is the Plain (newFileTemplate) one. The Plain template comes first. Response: a JSON array of {Name, Label, Plain, Builtin, Edited, Writable}.
    • GET /newtemplate?name=new/notes.tpl — One Template's Text Response: {Name, Label, Plain, Builtin, Edited, Writable, Text, Path}; Path is where saving writes it.
    • POST /newtemplate — Save a Template Body: {Name, Text, Base, From}. Name is new/<name>.tpl or a bare name; Base is the text the editor started from, and the save is refused (409) when the template has changed since; From, when it differs from Name, is the template this one is renamed from, whose own copy is removed. Refused (400) when the text does not parse, with Line and Col, or uses {% ssi %} or includes a file outside the template folders.
    • DELETE /newtemplate?name=new/notes.tpl — Delete a Template Removes this server's own copy; a built-in template of that name is used again. A built-in template with no copy cannot be deleted.
    • POST /newtemplate/preview — Render a Template That Is Not Saved Body: {Name, Text, Title, Filename, Answers}. Response: {Ok, Text, Fields} (Fields as /newtemplate/fields reads the text), or {Ok: false, Msg, Line, Col, Fields} saying where it broke.
    • GET /newtemplate/fields?name=new/meeting.tpl — What a Template Asks The template's ask("Client", "Acme") questions, in order, each once (an included template's in its place): {Name, Default}. The New File dialog shows a box for each and sends the answers as answers on POST /file.
    • GET /newtemplate/words — What a Template Can Name Every value (with what it would be now), function and filter, with what it does, for an editor to complete and explain.

    DELETE /attachment/{hash}/{name} — Throw One Away

    Removes the file from the heading's folder, and takes the line that linked to it out of the heading's body when that line was the link and nothing else.

    A link written into the middle of a sentence is left alone: the sentence is somebody's writing, and a hole in it is worse than a link to a file that has gone. A link alone on a line is litter once the file is gone.

    Method: DELETE

    Response: A Result JSON object. Msg says whether a link was taken out as well as the file.

    DELETE /dnd/play/session/{id}/mark — Take An Annotation Off

    Removes the annotation on one block of the timeline. The block itself is untouched - the rolls and notes it is made of stay exactly where they are.

    Method: DELETE

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    time string yes The clock the annotation is anchored on.
    kind string no The kind it was written against.

    An anchor that carries no annotation is refused with a 400 rather than quietly doing nothing, so a page working from a stale reading hears about it.

    Response: The session, read back in full.

    DELETE /dnd/play/session/{id}/note/{index} — Throw A Note Away

    Takes one note out of a session's notes altogether. The note is found the same way an edit finds it, and refused on the same terms.

    Method: DELETE

    Path Parameters:

    Parameter Type Description
    {id} string The session.
    {index} number Which note of that session, counting from zero.

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    was string no The stamp the note carried when the page read it.

    was is worth sending. Deleting a note shifts every note after it up by one, so a page holding stale numbers could otherwise throw away the wrong one and be none the wiser; when the stamp no longer matches, the call is refused with a 400 saying so.

    Response: The updated session record.

    DELETE /dnd/play/session/{id}/roll/{index} — Throw A Roll Away

    Takes one row out of a session's roll table. The row is found the same way an edit finds it, and refused on the same terms.

    Method: DELETE

    Path Parameters:

    Parameter Type Description
    {id} string The session.
    {index} number Which roll of that session, counting from zero.

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    was string no The label the roll carried when the page read it.

    As with a note, was is worth sending: deleting shifts every roll after it up by one, so a page holding stale numbers could otherwise throw away the wrong row.

    Taking the last row out takes the table with it, leaving the session exactly as it was before anything was rolled in it.

    Response: The updated session record.

    DELETE /dnd/session/{id} — Abandon a Character Build

    Throws the in progress character away.

    Method: DELETE

    DELETE /ext/capture/template — Delete a User Capture Template

    Deletes a per-user capture template by name. The change is persisted to the extensions YAML file.

    Method: DELETE

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    name string yes The name of the capture template to delete.

    Response: A ResultMsg JSON object confirming the deletion.

    Errors:

    • 401 if not authenticated.
    • 400 if name is missing.
    • 404 if the named template does not exist.

    DELETE /ext/kanban/board — Delete a Kanban Board

    Deletes one board by name. Only the board goes - a board is a way of looking at the org files and owns nothing in them, so no heading is touched.

    Method: DELETE

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    name string yes The name of the board to delete.

    Response: A ResultMsg JSON object confirming the deletion.

    Errors:

    • 401 if not authenticated.
    • 400 if name is missing.
    • 404 if no board has that name.

    DELETE /ext/query — Delete a Stored Query

    Deletes a stored query by name for the authenticated user. The change is persisted to the extensions YAML file.

    Method: DELETE

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    name string yes The name of the stored query to delete.

    Response: A ResultMsg JSON object confirming the deletion.

    Errors:

    • 401 if not authenticated.
    • 400 if name is missing.
    • 404 if the named query does not exist.

    DELETE /voice/recording/{id} — Throw a Recording Away

    Deletes one recording. This is not undoable and nothing else is touched: a note already filed keeps its heading and its transcript, and is left with an AUDIO link pointing at a file that is no longer there.

    Method: DELETE

    Path Parameters:

    Parameter Type Description
    id string The recording id.

    Response: A ResultMsg.

    Errors:

    • 401 if not authenticated.
    • 404 if there is no recording with that id.

    DELETE /watches — Stop Watching a Query

    Removes a watch by name. Its notifications stay in the list.

    Method: DELETE

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    name string yes The watch to remove.

    Response: The WatchList after the change; 404 when nothing has that name.

    GET /agenda — What Lands on Each Day

    The agenda worked out on the server: every heading that lands on each day of a range, with repeaters expanded, ranges spread over the days they span, overdue SCHEDULED items carried forward to today, and DEADLINE warnings. A client only draws it. The rules follow org's agenda:

    • A plain active timestamp (in the headline or the heading's own body, not a child's, not in a drawer) lands on its day. A repeater (+1w, ++1w, .+1w) lands on its base day and every interval after it; months and years keep to the calendar (Jan 31 +1m is Feb 28).
    • A range <a>--<b> lands on every day it spans, with the times written there on its first and last day and as all day between.
    • SCHEDULED lands on its day; not done and past, it also lands on today only, with Late days.
    • DEADLINE lands on its day; not done, it also lands on today inside its warning period (-Nd on the stamp, else agenda.deadlineWarningDays, default 14) with DueIn days, or past it with Late days.
    • A finished heading lands only on the days its dates name.
    • CLOSED lands on its day when closed=t.
    • A heading in an archived tree (tag ARCHIVE, here or above) is left out unless archived=t, as org's agenda skips archived trees.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    from date no First day, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.
    to date no Last day, inclusive. Defaults to from.
    today date no The day to count late and due from. The server's date.
    query string no Narrows the headings, as /search. Empty is all.
    closed bool no t adds CLOSED dates (the logbook view).
    archived bool no t keeps headings in archived trees.

    Response: An AgendaResult: ={"Ok": true, "From", "To", "Today", "Nodes": […], "Days": [{"Date", "Entries": [{"Node", "Kind", "Start", "End", "HasTime", "Repeat", "Late", "DueIn", "Done"}]}]}=. Node is an index into Nodes, so a heading on five days is sent once. Every day of the range is listed, empty or not. A bad date or query answers Ok: false with the reason in Msg.

    GET /agenda/nodes — Headings With Everything the Agenda Reads

    The headings a query finds (all of them with no query) as =AgendaNode=s - planning dates, timestamps, clocks, inherited tags, a summary of the children, the file's keywords - for list views that are not laid out by day: todo lists, projects, the clocked view.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    query string no The query expression, as for /search.

    Response: {"Ok": true, "Nodes": [...]}, or Ok: false and Msg.

    GET /agenda/print — The Agenda as a Printable Planner

    A self-contained html page to print (or to hand a headless Chrome, which is what orgs print -f pdf does): a week on one landscape sheet, a day on a portrait one, or a month as a calendar. What lands on each day is the /agenda answer for the same query, so paper and screen agree.

    • week: a spread - four days on the left page, three and a panel on the right. Each day lists its all day items (deadlines marked due, or in 3d while warning) and its timed ones, done items struck through, and ruled lines to write on. The panel has Overdue (what the agenda carries to today, late first), Tasks (undated open tasks, active ones first), a Habits strip with a box a day and Notes.
    • day: an hour grid (07:00 to 21:00, wider when something is earlier or later) with overlapping entries side by side, then the day's list, tasks, overdue and notes.
    • month: a calendar grid, a few entries a day and how many more.

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Description
    view week (default), day or month
    from a day in the first sheet, YYYY-MM-DD; today when empty
    pages sheets: weeks, days or months (default 1)
    days instead of pages: days to cover (week view: rounded up to weeks)
    query narrows the headings, as /agenda
    tasks the tasks panel's query; none for no panel
    habits f leaves the habits strip off
    theme classic (default), minimal, bullet, modern, or yours
    paper a4 (default) or letter
    weekstart mon (default) or sun
    today the day to count overdue from; the server's date
    list t answers the theme names, one a line

    A theme is one stylesheet in planner/themes/ on the template path; the layout is planner/base.css and the page planner/planner.html, and a copy of either in your template folder replaces it.

    Response: text/html, or a 400 with the reason as text.

    GET /assistant/status — The Writing Assistant's Backends

    Which AI backends the server offers worg's writing assistant, whether each has a key, its models, and the default: {Ok, Off, Default, Backends: [{Name, Label, Model, Models, Ready, Msg, Tools, Where, ModelWhere, Views, ViewTools}]}. Views says it may be used in worg's views and ViewTools that it can look up and change headings there. Where is where the writer's text is sent: machine (this one), network (another machine, by a private address or local name) or cloud; ModelWhere gives it per model for local, whose models may be on servers elsewhere. Off is true when assistant.backend is off. Keys are never sent; Source says where each one comes from (worg, orgs.yaml, environment, profile), and CanSetKeys whether this user may set them (POST /assistant/key).

    GET /attachment/{hash}/{name} — Fetch One

    The bytes of one attachment.

    Served by this server rather than as a path under /images because a heading's folder may be named by a :DIR: property pointing anywhere at all - including outside the org directory, where the static file server cannot reach. A url that works for some attachments and answers 404 for others is worse than one that always works.

    Method: GET

    Path Parameters:

    Parameter Description
    {hash} The heading, base64-url encoded as every hash in a path is
    {name} The file's name inside that heading's folder

    Response: The file, with a content type worked out from its extension. 404 when the heading owns no such file.

    GET /attachments — What a Heading Owns

    Everything in one heading's attachment folder.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    hash string yes The heading to ask about

    Response: An AttachList JSON object.

    Field Description
    Dir The folder, relative to the org root when it is inside it
    From dir when a :DIR: property named it, id when it came from the
    heading's :ID:, empty when the heading owns nothing yet
    Id The heading's id, empty when the folder came from a property
    Attachments The files, newest first

    A heading with no id and no :DIR: is not an error: it simply owns nothing yet, and From empty is how that is said. Nothing is created by asking.

    GET /attachments/all — Every Heading That Owns Files

    Walks the database for headings with an attachment folder and answers with what each of them owns, plus the totals - which is the question an attachment store eventually raises and which nothing else can answer.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    files string no t to include each heading's own file list. Off by
    default: the totals are the point and the lists are long.

    Response: An AttachAll JSON object holding Headings, Count, Size and Orphans.

    Orphans are folders under the attachment root that no heading claims - the heading was deleted, or its id changed, and the files were left behind. They are reported rather than cleaned up: they are somebody's files, and a server that deletes them because it cannot find a heading is a server that deletes them the first time a file fails to parse.

    GET /babel/sessions — The Python Sessions Running

    The sessions :session started, one per name per file: Name, File, Python (the command), Version, Pid, Runs, Started, LastUsed.

    GET /beamer/pdf — A File as a Beamer Deck, Compiled

    GET /beamer/pdf?filename=talk.org answers with the file as a beamer presentation, compiled to pdf (see Beamer under exporters). Its own endpoint, as /pdf and /book are, because the answer is bytes.

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Description
    filename the org file
    theme a preset (clean, dark, metropolis, classic, academic, minimal) or a beamer theme; wins over the file's
    code listings (the default) or minted
    refresh t compiles again rather than answering from the cache

    The latex is the beamer exporter's latex setting, else the pdf exporter's pdfLatex, else the first of pdflatex, xelatex and lualatex that is installed. A machine with no TeX answers 501 saying so; a deck that does not compile answers 422 with latex's first error.

    GET /beamer/themes — The Beamer Presets

    {"Ok": true, "Themes": ["clean", "dark", ...]}: the presets a deck can be exported in when its file names no #+BEAMER_THEME:. Any installed beamer theme's name works as well; these are the ones orgs dresses itself.

    GET /book — A File as a Manuscript (docx) or an Ebook (epub)

    GET /book?filename=story.org&to=docx answers with the file as a manuscript, to=epub as an ebook (see Manuscripts and Ebooks). Written by orgs itself, so nothing needs installing; the manuscript and epub exporters' settings are used when they are configured, and need not be.

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Description
    filename the org file
    to docx (or manuscript) or epub
    style the manuscript style: modern, shunn, novel, reader
    paper letter or a4
    theme the ebook theme: classic, literary, modern, plain
    list t answers {"Styles": [...], "Themes": [...]} instead

    Response: the file, with X-Orgs-Words (the word count) and, for an ebook, an X-Orgs-Warning header per picture that could not be put in.

    GET /code — Every Source Block

    Answers with every #+BEGIN_SRC block, read: its language, its name, its switches, its header arguments and its variables. A variable that names something else in the file - a table, another block, a list - comes back resolved, with what it points at and where that lives.

    Parameter Meaning
    lang Only blocks in this language
    q Only blocks matching this text

    The languages in use come back beside the blocks, with a count each, so a client can offer the filter without asking twice.

    GET /columns — Org Column View, With Rollups

    Answers with a file's outline as org's column view: the #+COLUMNS: line in force, the columns it names, and every heading with those properties filled in - including the summed value on any heading with children, for a column whose spec carries a summary operator.

    This is the only thing in orgs that adds EFFORT up. A %EFFORT{:} column makes a project heading show the total estimate of everything under it, which is a number nobody has to maintain.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Required Description
    file yes The org file to view.
    columns no A #+COLUMNS: line to use instead of the file's own.

    The line is taken from the first of these that says anything: the columns parameter, the file's own #+COLUMNS:, columns.default in the server config, and finally a built-in default. The answer says which in From.

    Summary operators: + and $ and : sum, min, max and mean pick, and any of them may carry a printf format after a semicolon (+;%.1f). A : prefix, and the EFFORT and CLOCKSUM columns whatever their operator, are read as durations and summed into H:MM. Org's checkbox operators (X, X/, X%) and its age operators (@min and friends) are not implemented and a column carrying one simply does not roll up.

    Response: A ColumnsResult. Each cell carries Value (what to show, which is the rollup on a summed parent), Own (what is written on that heading, which is what an edit changes) and Number (the value as a number, for sorting).

    Editing is through the endpoints that already exist: POST /property for an ordinary property, POST /status/change for TODO, POST /headline/change for ITEM. A cell's Kind on the spec says which.

    GET /columns/values — Every Property in a File, With Its Values

    Every property the file's headings use, on how many headings, and the unique values each takes with how often - most used first. The keyword, tags and priority come in as TODO, TAGS and PRIORITY. Behind the column view's value listing, its type-ahead while a cell is edited, and its property-name suggestions while a columns line is written.

    Method: GET

    Query: file - the org file.

    Response: A ColumnValuesResult: Ok, Msg, File, and Props, a list of {Name, Count, Values: [{Value, Count}]}.

    GET /contacts — Find Contacts

    /records?type=contact, with q searching names, numbers, addresses and notes alike.

    GET /crypt/config — Whether This Server Can Encrypt, and How

    Answers with the mode, the gpg it found, and how many headings carry the tag against how many of those are ciphertext right now.

    Method: GET

    Response: A CryptConfig JSON object.

    Field Description
    Mode off with no gpg, symmetric with no key, key with one
    Bin The gpg it will use
    Version What that gpg says about itself
    Key The key it encrypts to, in key mode
    Tag The tag that marks a heading for encryption
    Unlocked Whether a passphrase is being held, and UnlockIn for how much longer
    Tagged Headings carrying the tag
    Encrypted How many of those are ciphertext

    Tagged minus Encrypted is the number worth putting in front of somebody: headings that are meant to be secret and are sitting in the clear.

    GET /crypt/file — The Secret Headings in One File

    Every heading in one file carrying the crypt tag, in the order they are written, and whether each is ciphertext right now. Metadata only, as /crypt/headings is: what is secret, never what the secret is.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string yes The file, as /files names it

    Response: A CryptHeadings JSON object.

    GET /crypt/headings — What Is Marked Secret

    Every heading carrying the crypt tag, and whether each is ciphertext right now.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    plain string no t for only the ones sitting in the clear

    Response: A CryptHeadings JSON object holding Headings, Tagged and Plain.

    Never a body. A listing says what is secret, not what the secret is - an endpoint that handed over plaintext because it was convenient would undo the feature for every client that ever called it.

    GET /crypt/state — Is a Passphrase Held Right Now

    The cheap half of /crypt/config: no gpg is run and no file is read, so a lock indicator can ask every few seconds.

    Method: GET

    Response: A CryptState JSON object.

    Field Description
    Mode off, symmetric or key
    Tag The tag that marks a heading for encryption
    Unlocked Whether a passphrase is held, and UnlockIn for how long
    UnlockSeconds crypt.unlockSeconds: zero means nothing is ever held

    GET /csv — A Column View or a Query as CSV

    GET /csv?file=project.org answers with the file's column view as csv: the #+COLUMNS: line in force (or columns=), one row per heading, and the rolled-up value on a parent for a summed column (%EFFORT{:}), as worg's Columns tab and orgs cols show it.

    GET /csv?query=IsTodo() answers with the headings a query finds instead, one row each and nothing summed, in the columns %ITEM %TODO %PRIORITY %TAGS %SCHEDULED %DEADLINE %EFFORT %CLOCKSUM %FILE unless columns= names others. Filters ({{WorkTasks}}) work as in /search.

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Description
    file the org file whose column view to write
    query the query whose headings to write (instead of file)
    columns a #+COLUMNS: line to use
    sep comma (default), semicolon or tab
    header f leaves off the header row
    bom t starts with a byte order mark, for Excel
    meta t adds Level, Line and Hash (and File) columns
    own t writes each heading's own value, not a parent's rollup

    Response: text/csv, named after the file (or query.csv); a problem is a plain-text 400 or 404.

    GET /dblocks — The Dynamic Blocks In A File

    GET /dblocks?file=/path/notes.org lists every #+BEGIN: block in the file: its name, its header and parameters, the rows of its BEGIN and END lines (zero based) and the heading it sits under. Without file, every file that has one is listed.

    GET /dnd/books — List Files Written as D&D Books

    Answers with every org file the server is watching that asks to be printed as a D&D book - that is, one carrying #+LATEX_CLASS: dndbook. This is the book-shaped sibling of /dnd/characters: a client showing a file can use it to know whether to offer the book views for that file.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters: none

    Response: A JSON array, one entry per file.

    Field Type Description
    filename string The absolute path the server knows the file by
    title string Its #+TITLE:, when it has one
    class string The latex class it asked for 
    [{"filename": "/org/dnd_pdf_example.org", "title": "The Sunken Tower", "class": "dndbook"}]

    GET /dnd/campaigns — Campaigns

    Every campaign under the org directories: an org file with #+CAMPAIGN: t (or campaign in its #+FILETAGS:). Its #+TITLE: names it, #+CAMPAIGN_ICON: is its icon (an emoji) and #+CAMPAIGN_ART: its picture (relative to the file, fetched with GET /dnd/dungeon/image); the text before the first heading describes it. Each heading tagged :area: is an area - a section of the world - and the links to org files in its own text are its maps, in order.

    Method: GET

    Response: {Ok, Campaigns: [{file, title, icon, art, description, modified, areas: [{name, line, maps: [{file, title, link, missing}]}]}]}, newest first. missing is a link to no map (moved, or a file with no .dungeon.json beside it).

    GET /dnd/catalog — Browse Ruleset Content

    Lists the valid choices of one kind from a ruleset, with the summary and detail text the interactive builder shows. This is what powers "what are my options?" in a client.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    kind string yes races, classes, subclasses, backgrounds, spells, items, feats, skills, languages
    ruleset string no Ruleset id, defaults to srd.
    id string no For subclasses the class id, for spells the class to filter by.
    filter string no Case insensitive substring match on the name.

    Response: CatalogResponse, an array of options each with id, name, summary, detail, tags and meta.

    GET /dnd/characters — List Known Character Sheets

    Scans the org database for files tagged as dnd character sheets and returns a one line summary of each.

    Method: GET

    Response:

    [{"filename": "/gtd/lyra.org", "name": "Lyra", "race": "High Elf",
  "class": "Wizard (School of Evocation) 3", "level": 3, "ac": 12, "hp": 20}]

    GET /dnd/concentration — What A Caster Is Holding

    Returns the spell a character is concentrating on, if any, along with the Constitution saving throw they make to keep it. Nothing is changed.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string no The org character sheet (basename or path).
    id string no The character's DND_ID, used when no filename.

    One of the two is required.

    Response: A ConcentrationState:

    {"id": "lyra-silverleaf-4c1f2a", "name": "Lyra", "filename": "/gtd/lyra.org",
 "ruleset": "srd",
 "concentration": {"on": true, "spell": "haste", "name": "Haste", "level": 3,
                   "label": "Haste (3rd level)", "duration": "1 minute",
                   "saveMod": 2, "saveStr": "+2"}}

    on is false when nothing is being held, which is the usual state: the banner has to be able to draw its own absence.

    GET /dnd/conditions — What A Character Is Under, And What They Shrug Off

    Returns the conditions currently on a character, every condition they could be under, the damage they take less, none or more of, and the sheet's Condition History. Nothing is changed - this is what the character sheet's defenses tab is drawn from, including the condition picker.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string no The org character sheet (basename or path).
    id string no The character's DND_ID, used when no filename.

    One of the two is required.

    Response: A ConditionsState:

    {
  "id": "lyra-silverleaf-4c1f2a", "name": "Lyra", "filename": "/gtd/lyra.org",
  "conditions": {
    "active": [{"id": "frightened", "name": "Frightened", "on": true,
                "label": "Frightened"},
               {"id": "exhaustion", "name": "Exhaustion", "on": true, "level": 2,
                "levels": 6, "label": "Exhaustion 2", "note": "Speed halved"}],
    "all": [{"id": "blinded", "name": "Blinded", "icon": "blinded", "on": false,
             "text": "A blinded creature can't see..."}],
    "count": 2, "summary": "Frightened, Exhaustion 2"
  },
  "defenses": {
    "resistances": [{"id": "fire", "name": "Fire", "kind": "resistance", "damage": true}],
    "immunities": [], "vulnerabilities": [], "any": true,
    "summary": "resistant to fire"
  },
  "damageTypes": [{"id": "acid", "name": "Acid"}],
  "history": [{"date": "2025-09-05", "time": "21:14", "action": "gained",
               "name": "Frightened", "notes": "the wraith's shriek"}]
}

    conditions.all is the whole catalog with on set, which is what the picker needs; conditions.active is the same entries filtered down to what is on. Only exhaustion has levels, and then note is the line the level in force carries. damageTypes is the ruleset's catalog, so a sheet can offer them without carrying its own copy.

    GET /dnd/dungeon — The Dungeon Generator's Settings

    The settings form of the random dungeon generator and the props the editor can place.

    Method: GET

    Response: {ok, fields: [...], props: [...]}, fields as GET /dnd/generate describes them.

    GET /dnd/dungeon/image — A Dungeon's Picture

    The picture a dungeon is shown as (a Dungeon Alchemist export, or any image), by the path its data keeps, relative to the dungeon's org file.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    file string yes The dungeon's org file.
    path string yes The picture, relative to it (maps/x-map.jpg).

    A path starting @shared/ is in the shared folder (dndSharedPath) instead: its tokens, tiles or images, pictures or (tokens, tiles) videos.

    Response: the picture.

    GET /dnd/dungeon/load — Open a Saved Dungeon

    The data of a dungeon saved by POST /dnd/dungeon/save, for the editor.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    file string yes The dungeon's org file (or its .dungeon.json).

    Response: {ok, dungeon, exits, state}, state being the fog of war and the party's pin (see POST /dnd/dungeon/state).

    GET /dnd/dungeon/pictures — A Map's Pictures to Show

    Every picture in the images folder beside a map's org file, and in its subfolders, which are its categories (images/npcs/, images/monsters/…). Fetch one with GET /dnd/dungeon/image and its path.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    file string yes The map's org file.
    folder string no images (the default), tokens or tiles.

    Response: {Ok, Dir, Pictures: [{path, name, category, size, still, shared}], Categories, Shared}; no folder is an empty list, not an error. A token's size is large when its folder's tokens.json says so. The shared folder's (dndSharedPath) come after the map's own, their paths starting @shared/; Shared says whether there is one. A token may be a video (.webm, .mp4), with still the picture of the same name beside it. A tile's size is its squares (3x2), as remembered or as its file's name says (Room_3x2.png), else empty. tags are the GM's words for it, kept in the folder's json (tokens.json, tiles.json, images.json).

    GET /dnd/dungeon/saved — Saved Dungeons

    The dungeons saved under the org directories, newest first, by their .dungeon.json files.

    Method: GET

    Response: {ok, dungeons: [{file, name, modified}]}, file being the org file.

    GET /dnd/generate — List the Random Generators

    The generators the random generator offers (encounters, traps, treasure, magic items, spellbooks, NPCs, taverns, trinkets and so on), each with the options its form takes. A race option's choices are the ruleset's races.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    ruleset string no Ruleset id; the default ruleset when absent.

    Response: {ok, generators: [{id, name, group, summary, count, fields: [{id, label, kind, choices, default}]}]}

    GET /dnd/hp — Where A Character Stands

    Returns the hit point line: current, maximum, the temporary hit points in front of them, how full the bar is, and the sheet's Health History.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string no The org character sheet (basename or path).
    id string no The character's DND_ID, used when no filename.

    One of the two is required.

    Response: A HealthState:

    {
  "id": "lyra-silverleaf-4c1f2a", "name": "Lyra", "filename": "/gtd/lyra.org",
  "hp": {"current": 14, "max": 27, "temp": 5, "percent": 51, "tempPercent": 18,
         "down": false, "bloodied": true, "deathSaves": ""},
  "history": [{"date": "2025-09-05", "time": "21:40", "action": "hurt",
               "amount": 9, "absorbed": 5, "hpBefore": 18, "hpAfter": 14,
               "tempBefore": 5, "tempAfter": 0, "hpMax": 27,
               "notes": "wraith's touch"}]
}

    GET /dnd/inspiration — Whether A Character Holds Inspiration

    Returns whether a character is currently holding inspiration. Nothing is changed.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string no The org character sheet (basename or path).
    id string no The character's DND_ID, used when no filename.

    One of the two is required.

    Response: An InspirationState:

    {"id": "lyra-silverleaf-4c1f2a", "name": "Lyra", "filename": "/gtd/lyra.org",
 "ruleset": "srd", "inspiration": true, "msg": ""}

    GET /dnd/inventory — What A Character Is Carrying

    Returns the equipment table stacked into containers, the weight carried, where that lands on the encumbrance scale, and the sheet's Inventory History.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string no The org character sheet (basename or path).
    id string no The character's DND_ID, used when no filename.

    One of the two is required.

    Response: An InventoryState:

    {
  "id": "lyra-silverleaf-4c1f2a", "name": "Lyra", "filename": "/gtd/lyra.org",
  "inventory": {
    "containers": [
      {"key": "", "name": "On Person", "weight": 21, "entries": [
        {"key": "backpack", "name": "Backpack", "qty": 1, "weight": 5, "isContainer": true}]},
      {"key": "backpack", "name": "Backpack", "capacity": 30, "weight": 16, "entries": []}
    ],
    "weight": 37, "carryCapacity": 150, "encumberedAt": 50,
    "level": "", "label": "Unencumbered"
  },
  "history": [{"date": "2025-09-05", "time": "19:32", "action": "added",
               "item": "Potion of Healing", "qty": 2, "to": "Backpack"}],
  "ac": 16, "acSource": "+2 Leather"
}

    Each entry carries wearable and usable, which say whether the line is something that can be worn or wielded and whether it is something that is spent by being used. Armour, shields and weapons are wearable but never usable.

    An entry that requires attunement says attunement, an entry whose text says plainly what using one up does carries use (see below), and one the rules put a price on carries price and sale, so the panel can offer to buy, sell or drink a line without having to price or read anything itself.

    ac and acSource are the armour class the character is left with, so a sheet that wears or removes armour can redraw its armour class without loading again. purse, moneyHistory, attunement and hp ride along for the same reason: buying moves the coin, attuning moves what is live, and drinking a potion moves the hit points.

    GET /dnd/items — Fuzzy Item Search

    Searches the items of a ruleset the way the character builder's list filter does: every term has to match and letters may be skipped, so pot heal finds a Potion of Healing and bkpk finds a Backpack. This is what the add item box on the html character sheet asks.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    q string no The search. Empty returns the front of the list.
    ruleset string no Ruleset to search, defaults to the character's or srd.
    filename string no Character sheet, so hits can say how many you own.
    id string no The character's DND_ID, same purpose.
    containers bool no Only return containers.
    filter string no Group to search in, see below. Defaults to all.
    limit number no Maximum hits, default 40.

    The filter narrows the pool the search runs over to one group of things: all, weapon, armor, potion, focus (spellcasting foci and components), gear, tool, pack, container or magic (anything with a rarity). A name none of them goes by is an error rather than a silent all.

    Response:

    [{"id": "potion-of-healing", "name": "Potion of Healing", "kind": "gear",
  "cost": "50 gp", "weight": 0.5, "rarity": "Common", "owned": 2,
  "text": "You regain 2d4 + 2 hit points when you drink this potion."}]

    GET /dnd/journal — The DM's Notes on a Map

    Every org heading tied to a spot on a map: a heading with :DND_AT: x y (squares of the plan) whose DND_MAP - its own, a parent's, or the file's #+DND_MAP: keyword - names the map (relative to the file it is written in; a bare path, file:path or an org link). Any org file may hold them, but not the map's own, which is written again from the map's data on every save.

    Method: GET

    Query: file the map's org file.

    Response: {Ok, Entries: [{file, rel, line, end, level, title, x, y, colour, text}], Journal}: line the heading's line (zero based), end the line after its subtree, text the subtree, Journal the file new notes go into (<map>-journal.org beside the map).

    GET /dnd/map/thumb — A Map's Thumbnail

    A small picture of a map, for lists: its picture (a picture dungeon's, a generated map's) shrunk to w pixels across (default 360, at most 800) as a JPEG, made once and kept in the user cache until the picture changes; a WebP picture is sent as it is. A dungeon drawn by the generator has its saved drawing (maps/name-map.svg) sent as it is - an svg is small and scales.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters: file (the map's org file), w.

    Response: the picture, or 404 when the map has none.

    GET /dnd/maps — Every Map

    Every map and dungeon under the org directories - each org file with a .dungeon.json beside it, what the file view offers its Map view for - for the campaign window's list.

    Method: GET

    Response: {Ok, Maps: [{file, rel, name, world, modified}]}, rel the file's path under its org directory, name the map's own (else the file's #+TITLE:, else its name), newest first.

    GET /dnd/money — What A Character Is Carrying In Coin

    Returns the purse broken down by denomination, what the lot is worth, what it weighs, and the sheet's Coin History.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string no The org character sheet (basename or path).
    id string no The character's DND_ID, used when no filename.

    One of the two is required.

    Response: A MoneyState:

    {
  "id": "lyra-silverleaf-4c1f2a", "name": "Lyra", "filename": "/gtd/lyra.org",
  "purse": {
    "coins": [
      {"id": "pp", "name": "Platinum", "abbr": "pp", "qty": 1, "value": 1000, "gold": 10},
      {"id": "gp", "name": "Gold", "abbr": "gp", "qty": 42, "value": 100, "gold": 42}
    ],
    "money": {"cp": 5, "sp": 0, "ep": 0, "gp": 42, "pp": 1},
    "copper": 5205, "gold": 52.05, "total": "52 gp 5 cp", "count": 48, "weight": 0.96
  },
  "history": [{"date": "2025-09-05", "time": "19:32", "action": "spent",
               "amount": {"gp": 50}, "balance": {"gp": 42, "pp": 1, "cp": 5},
               "notes": "potion of healing"}]
}

    A coin is worth what it is worth in D&D: one gold piece is 100 cp, 10 sp, 2 ep or a tenth of a platinum, and fifty coins of any kind weigh a pound.

    GET /dnd/monster — A Monster's Stat Block

    One SRD monster by name, as written in a room or a wandering monster table ("Goblins" and "goblin" both find the goblin): its stat block - ability scores, speed, saves, senses and the like, traits, actions, reactions and legendary actions - and its initiative bonus.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    name string yes The monster's name.

    Response: {ok, monster, init}

    GET /dnd/monsters — Find Monsters

    SRD monsters whose names hold every word of q, those starting with it first, each with what an initiative tracker needs to add one: armour class, hit points, initiative bonus.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    q string no Words of the name.
    limit int no At most this many (40).

    Response: {ok, monsters: [{id, name, cr, xp, ac, hp, hitDice, type, size, init}]}

    GET /dnd/music — The Music Folder

    Every track in the music folder (dndMusicPath), with the folder each is in as its album (a zip, 7z, rar or tar is a folder of its own), sorted by album and name. Fetch one with GET /dnd/music/file.

    Method: GET

    Response: {Ok, Msg, Dir, Tracks: [{path, name, album}], Albums: [{name, count}]}

    GET /dnd/music/file — A Track

    A track from the music folder by its path (@music/...), out of an archive when its path runs through one, turned into Ogg Opus first when a browser could not play it.

    Method: GET

    Response: the track.

    GET /dnd/music/spotify — Spotify, as the DM Screen Sees It

    Whether the Spotify app is on this machine and playing (and what), whether Spotify's Web API is set up (spotifyClientId) and signed in, and the redirect URI to give Spotify's app.

    Method: GET

    Response: {Ok, App, Configured, Connected, Redirect, State: {running, playing, track, artist, album, uri, duration, position, volume}}

    GET /dnd/music/spotify/login — Sign In to Spotify

    Sends the browser to Spotify to let orgs search and read the DM's playlists (PKCE: no secret). Spotify sends it back to /dnd/music/spotify/callback, which keeps the sign in.

    Method: GET

    GET /dnd/music/spotify/playlists — The DM's Spotify Playlists

    The signed in DM's playlists, their own and followed, up to two hundred.

    Method: GET

    Response: {Ok, Items: [{kind, name, by, uri, image, count}]}

    GET /dnd/music/spotify/search — Search Spotify

    Tracks, albums and playlists for q, through the Web API (signed in).

    Method: GET

    Response: {Ok, Items: [{kind, name, by, uri, image, duration, count}]}

    GET /dnd/party — The Party

    The party the initiative tracker plays with, from the org file this user chose for it (POST /dnd/party/file): a heading per character with DND_PC, PLAYER, AC, HP, INIT, LEVEL, CLASS, PASSIVE and SHEET properties. A member with a SHEET has its numbers read from that character sheet.

    Method: GET

    Response: {ok, file, members: [...]}, file empty when none has been chosen yet.

    GET /dnd/play/session/{id}/undo — What Undo Would Take Back In This Session

    Answers what the last change to one session file was, and whether it can be reversed. Nothing is changed; this is what the timeline asks so its Undo offer can say what pressing it will do.

    This is the character sheet's undo journal narrowed to one file. The sheet's own Undo button takes back the last thing that happened anywhere; a drawer showing one evening should offer to take back the last thing that happened to that evening, so that deleting a block and then rolling a die does not leave the timeline offering to un-roll the die.

    Method: GET

    Response: An UndoPlan, can false with a why when there is nothing to take back.

    The journal is memory only and holds the last thirty changes this server made, so a restart empties it. There is no history to fall back on here the way there is for a character sheet: a session file records what happened at the table, and nothing in it is derived from anything that could be worked backwards.

    GET /dnd/rulesets — List Loaded D&D Rulesets

    Returns every ruleset the dnd module has loaded, including the built in SRD data and any add on yaml modules found on the configured dndPaths.

    Method: GET

    Parameters: None.

    Response: A JSON array of ruleset summaries:

    [
  {
    "id": "srd",
    "name": "SRD 5.1 Core Rules",
    "version": "5.1",
    "modules": ["builtin:srd-core.yaml", "/Users/me/dnd/homebrew.yaml"],
    "races": 9, "classes": 12, "backgrounds": 13, "spells": 319, "items": 201
  }
]

    GET /dnd/session/{id} — Current Character Creation Prompt

    Returns the prompt the session is waiting on, which is how a client resumes an interrupted character build.

    Method: GET

    Response: A Prompt, or 404 when the session has expired.

    GET /dnd/sheet — Computed Character Sheet

    Parses an org character sheet and returns everything derived from it: ability modifiers, saving throws, all eighteen skills, armour class, initiative, hit dice, attacks, spell save DC, spell slots, carrying capacity and the collected feature text.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string yes The org character sheet (basename or path).

    Response: A Sheet object. Anything the engine could not resolve (an unknown class id for example) is reported in the warnings array rather than failing the request.

    GET /dnd/sounds — The Sound Folder

    Every sound in the sound folder (dndSoundPath): its subfolders are categories, and a zip, 7z, rar or tar in it is read as a folder. Fetch one with GET /dnd/sounds/file.

    Method: GET

    Response: {Ok, Dir, Sounds: [{path, name, category, source, page, license}], Categories}; no folder set is Ok false.

    GET /dnd/sounds/file — A Sound

    A sound from the sound folder by its path (@sounds/..., as GET /dnd/sounds gives it), out of an archive when its path runs through one.

    Method: GET

    Response: the sound.

    GET /dnd/sounds/search — Search the Web for Sounds

    Searches every sound service that lets a sound be played and downloaded without an account at once - Freesound (previews), BBC Sound Effects, Tabletop Audio, Mixkit, SoundBible, Soundgator and Openverse - and answers what each found, a service that fails or is slow (nine seconds) left out with its reason.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters: q, what to look for.

    Response: {Ok, Sounds: [{source, name, url, page, license, author, duration, cached}], Failed: {service: why}}

    GET /dnd/undo — What Undo Would Take Back

    Answers what the last thing that happened to a character was, and whether it can be reversed. Nothing is changed; this is what the html sheet asks so its Undo button can say what pressing it will do rather than offering a bare "Undo".

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string no The org character sheet (basename or path).
    id string no The character's DND_ID, used when no filename.

    One of the two is required.

    Response: An UndoPlan:

    {"can": true, "what": "using Potion of Healing and the hit points it moved",
 "when": "2026-09-18 19:32", "kind": "used"}

    When can is false, why says what is in the way in the words the sheet shows - "the hit points have moved since", "nothing has happened yet".

    GET /drill/cards — The Cards of a Flashcard Deck

    Runs a deck's query and answers with every card it found, each with its question and answer drawn as html, where it stands (new, failed, overdue, young, old, or not due), and how many days each rating 0-5 would put it away for. This is worg's Drill tab's one read; the session itself - which card next, the again pile, the limits - runs in the browser.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Description
    deck A saved deck's name (see /ext/drill/decks).
    query Or a query expression, for a deck that is not saved.
    algorithm With query: sm5 (default), sm2 or simple8.
    cram 1 for cram mode: everything not seen in the last 12 hours is due.
    theme The html theme to draw the cards in; the reply's style is its css.
    format org for the cards' org text instead of html (orgs drill draws it).

    Response: {ok, msg, deck, query, cards: [DrillCard], counts, problems, style}. A card that cannot be drilled (an unknown DRILL_CARD_TYPE, an empty body) is left out and named in problems.

    GET /editor/help — The File Editor's Keys and Snippets

    The help for worg's Files tab editor (keys, snippets, org commands), from the org file embedded in the server at build time, rendered to html.

    Method: GET

    Response: {"Ok": true, "Html": "..."}

    GET /events — Watch for Changes

    A long-lived connection that says when something changed. One JSON object per event, in text/event-stream format (server-sent events), so a browser reads it with EventSource and a terminal reads it with curl -N.

    This is what makes a live view possible at all: the server has always watched the org files and until now had no way to tell anybody.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    kinds string no Comma separated event kinds to send; everything by default.

    Event kinds:

    Kind Meaning
    hello Sent once when the stream opens.
    reload An org file was re-read; anything from it may have moved.
    clockin A clock was started on a heading.
    clockout The running clock was stopped.
    focusstart, focusend, breakstart, breakend, focusstop, focusextend A focus session moved on; see /focus/start.
    querymatch A watched query gained (or lost) headings; watch, label, count, notice, headings, left. Only to the watch's owner. See /watches.
    notify A notification ready to show: title, msg (the body), url (where a click goes), group (replaces the last of its group), urgency (low, normal, critical), sound. Reminders, the deadline digest, watches with desktop, focus phases.

    Response: text/event-stream. Each event is a data: line holding one JSON object, followed by a blank line. A : comment line arrives every twenty seconds as a heartbeat, which keeps proxies from closing an idle stream.

    data: {"kind":"hello","index":41,"at":"2026-09-27T23:00:00-07:00"}

data: {"kind":"reload","file":"/home/me/org/todo.org","index":42,"at":"2026-09-27T23:01:12-07:00"}

    GET /ext/capture/templates — List User Capture Templates

    Returns the per-user capture templates for the authenticated user. These are in addition to the server-wide templates defined in config. Per-user templates are stored in the extensions YAML file.

    Method: GET

    Parameters: None (user identity is derived from the auth token).

    Response: A JSON array of CaptureTemplate objects. Returns an empty array if the user has no custom templates.

    Errors: 401 if not authenticated.

    GET /ext/drill/decks — List Flashcard Decks

    Every flashcard deck the user has saved, in the order worg shows them. A deck is a query that picks its cards and org-drill's settings for drilling them (algorithm, session limits, leech handling…). It holds no cards.

    Method: GET

    Response: A JSON array of DrillDeck objects.

    GET /ext/gantt/views — List Saved Gantt Views

    Every gantt chart setup the user has saved: the query it draws, the renderer, colours, swim lane property, calendar window and marker lines.

    Method: GET

    Response: A JSON array of GanttView objects.

    GET /ext/kanban/boards — List Kanban Boards

    Returns every kanban board the authenticated user has saved, in the order they are shown as tabs. A board says where its cards come from (a stored query name or a query expression), what splits them into columns, and how they are drawn. It holds no cards itself - those are worked out from the query each time the board is opened. Boards live in the per-user extensions YAML file.

    Method: GET

    Parameters: None (user identity is derived from the auth token).

    Response: A JSON array of KanbanBoard objects:

    [{"name": "Notes", "storedQuery": "All Notes", "groupBy": "property",
  "groupKey": "STAGE", "columns": [{"value": "idea", "title": "Ideas"}],
  "colorBy": "property", "colorKey": "AREA", "sort": "manual",
  "orderKey": "KANBAN"}]

    Returns an empty array if the user has no boards.

    Errors: 401 if not authenticated.

    GET /ext/queries — List Stored Queries

    Returns all stored queries for the authenticated user. Stored queries are named search expressions that users can save for quick recall. They are persisted in the per-user extensions YAML file.

    Method: GET

    Parameters: None (user identity is derived from the auth token).

    Response: A JSON array of StoredQuery objects:

    [{"name": "My Tasks", "query": "TODO=\"TODO\"+HOME"}]

    Returns an empty array if the user has no stored queries.

    Errors: 401 if not authenticated.

    GET /ext/query — Get a Stored Query by Name

    Returns a single stored query for the authenticated user, looked up by name.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    name string yes The name of the stored query.

    Response: A StoredQuery JSON object: {"name": "...", "query": "..."}.

    Errors:

    • 401 if not authenticated.
    • 400 if name is missing.
    • 404 if the named query does not exist.

    GET /file/delete — May I Delete Files?

    Answers whether the logged-in account may delete org files, so a client can offer the action only to somebody who may use it.

    Method: GET

    Response: {"Ok": true, "CanDelete": true}, with Msg saying why not when CanDelete is false.

    POST /file/delete — Delete Org Files

    Deletes org files from disk and forgets them. For an administrator, or an account marked delete: true in the keystore (orgs user candelete <name>); anyone when noAuth is on. Each file must be one the server reads and must sit inside one of the orgDirs. A file that cannot be deleted does not stop the others.

    Method: POST

    Request Body (JSON):

    Field Type Required Description
    Files string[] yes Absolute paths, as /files gives them.

    Response: {"Ok", "Msg", "Deleted": [...], "Failed": {"path": "why"}}. Ok is true only when every file was deleted. Refused with 403 when the account may not delete.

    GET /files/search — Search the Text of Every Org File

    A regular-expression search over the raw text of every org file the server is watching, answering with the lines that matched and where they are.

    This is the text-level sibling of /search: that one queries the parsed database and understands headings, keywords and dates; this one reads lines and understands nothing, which is what finds a phrase written in a drawer, a table or a source block.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    q string yes The regular expression (Go syntax)
    ignoreCase string no t to match without regard to case
    max number no Matching lines kept per file (default 40, capped at 500)
    file string no Only search this file (basename or path)

    Response: A FileSearchResult JSON object.

    Field Type Description
    Ok bool False when the pattern does not compile
    Msg string Why it does not compile
    Files array One entry per file with at least one match
    FileCount number How many files matched
    Total number How many lines matched, across every file

    Each file carries Filename, Count (every matching line, even the ones past the cap), Truncated, and Matches of Line (zero based), Text, Start and End.

    A pattern that does not compile answers 200 with Ok: false, because a half-typed pattern is an ordinary state of a box somebody is typing in rather than a failed request.

    GET /files/themes — List Files That Name Their Own Html Theme

    Answers with every org file carrying #+HTML_THEME:, and the theme it asks for. A file that says how it wants to be read is asking for something the reader's own theme setting would otherwise override, so a client showing it can offer that reading as a view of its own.

    The theme is reported as the file wrote it, whether or not this server has a stylesheet by that name - /html/themes is the list of the ones it has, and answering with only those would silently swallow a typo.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters: none

    Response: A JSON array, one entry per file.

    Field Type Description
    filename string The absolute path the server knows the file by
    theme string The theme it asked for
    title string Its #+TITLE:, when it has one 
    [{"filename": "/org/docs.org", "theme": "docs", "title": "Orgs"}]

    GET /focus — The Focus Session Now

    What the focus (pomodoro) session is doing: working on a heading, on a break, or idle. /focus/state is the same thing.

    Method: GET

    Response: A FocusState:

    Field Meaning
    Phase work, break or idle.
    LongBreak The break under way is a long one.
    Hash, Title, File The task. When idle, the last task, to offer another on it.
    Started, Ends RFC3339; empty when idle.
    Remaining, Total Seconds left and seconds in the phase, counted by the server.
    Now The server's time, so a client with a wrong clock can allow for it.
    Streak Pomodoros finished since the last long break.
    Today, TodayMinutes Pomodoros finished today, and minutes of focus today.
    Settings {Work, Short, Long, LongEvery, AutoNext}, minutes.

    The hash is worked out afresh on each answer, since clocking out writes to the heading's file and can change it.

    GET /focus/history — Focus Sessions Lately

    The work phases of the last few days, newest first: each with its heading, start and end, minutes, whether it was finished (Completed) or stopped, and the break that followed. Thirty days are kept.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    days int no How many days, today included. Default 1.

    Response: {"Ok": true, "Today": 3, "TodayMinutes": 80, "Records": [...]}

    GET /forge/check — Whether the GitHub and GitLab Tokens Work

    Asks each github and gitlab poller's api who its token belongs to, writing nothing. orgs forge check calls it.

    Method: GET

    Response: A ForgeReply as for POST /forge/sync, each result's User the login the token belongs to, or Ok false and the api's refusal in Msg.

    GET /habits — Every Habit, And How It Is Going

    Answers with every heading carrying :STYLE: habit, its cadence, and its recent history: the current run, the best run it has ever been on, how much of what the cadence asked for actually happened, and one entry per day for the last few weeks.

    The history is read out of the State "DONE" lines in each heading's logbook - the ones POST /status/change writes. Before orgs wrote them this endpoint could only have answered about habits kept in Emacs.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Required Description
    days no How many days of history, 7 to 371. Default 56.

    Response: A HabitsResult. Each habit's Days runs oldest first and ends on today, with a State of done, miss or ok:

    • done — a completion is recorded that day.
    • miss — as of that day, more time had passed than the habit allows.
    • ok — neither: inside the grace the habit's own repeater grants.

    Three states rather than two because "not done" means two different things. A daily habit not done yesterday is a broken run; a habit written .+1d/3d not done yesterday is a day you had in hand. Drawing both the same way makes a well-kept habit look like a failing one. For the same reason the day a habit comes round is never a miss - you have that day to do it - and no day before the habit's first ever completion is one either.

    Rate is counted from the habit's first completion rather than from the edge of the window, so a habit started on Tuesday and kept since reads as kept rather than as 4%.

    DoneKeyword is the first finished keyword of that heading's own file, so a tracker can offer a button to tick the habit off without a request per habit. Ticking it off is POST /status/change as usual, which moves the repeater on and writes the logbook line that this endpoint reads back.

    GET /harper/status — Harper on the Server

    {Ok, Enabled, State, Msg}: whether the server offers Harper, and whether harper-ls is off (not yet asked for), starting, ready or failed, and why.

    GET /history — A File's Git History

    Whether an org file is under git, what is uncommitted, and the commits that touched it, newest first, with parents rewritten to that history so a client can draw it as a graph. Used by worg's Diff tab.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    file string yes An org file the server reads.
    limit int no How many commits at most (default 300).
    all bool no Every branch, not just the one checked out.

    Response: Ok, Msg, InRepo, Repo, Path, Branch, Head, Last (the newest commit from HEAD that touched the file), Untracked, Staged / StagedAdd / StagedDel, Modified / ModifiedAdd / ModifiedDel, Truncated, and Commits: each with Hash, Short, Parents, Author, Email, When (unix seconds), Subject, Refs, and the lines it Added and Removed in this file. A file not under git answers Ok with InRepo false.

    GET /history/text — An Org File at a Revision

    The text of an org file at a git revision, as staged, or on disk.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    file string yes An org file the server reads.
    rev string no A commit or ref, INDEX, or WORKING (the default).

    Response: Ok, Msg, Rev, Text, and Missing when the file did not exist at that revision (Text is then empty, and Ok still true).

    GET /insights/deps — Dependency Health

    What is wrong with the AFTER and ORDERED links between headings, read with the gantt's own rules (an AFTER names a heading by hash, ID or CUSTOM_ID as written; an ORDERED parent chains each child behind the one before; NOBLOCKING takes a child out). Each problem is one of:

    Kind What it means
    cycle Headings that wait on each other in a circle (each reported once), a heading
    AFTER its own ancestor, or one sharing its parent's hash.
    waiting-on-done WAITING (or BLOCKED, HOLD…) on a heading that is finished.
    blocked-chain Open headings held up behind one open root blocker: reported when the longest
    chain is min long or more, or when the root is itself WAITING.
    dangling An AFTER naming no heading, or an archived one.
    ordered-stuck An ORDERED project whose current step is WAITING, or with a later step done
    ahead of it.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    query string no Only problems involving a heading this finds. Links are always
    followed through the whole database.
    min int no Shortest blocked chain worth reporting. Default 3.

    Response: A DepReport: Problems (errors first, then warnings, then notes), Counts per kind and Checked. Each problem has Kind, Severity, Title, Suggestion, Length, Held (blocked chains), Missing (dangling) and Chain: the headings in work order, what is waited on first (a cycle ends where it began). Each heading carries its hash, file, line, keyword, Via (AFTER or ORDERED: how it waits on the one before) and After, NoBlocking and Chained, which are what a client needs to take that wait away.

    GET /insights/estimates — How Far Off Are the Estimates

    EFFORT against the clock. Every finished task with both an EFFORT and clocked time is measured: its actual (every clock it has, plus the clocks of headings under it with no EFFORT of their own) over its estimate. The tasks are then grouped, and each group gets its totals, the median and the middle half (25th to 75th percentile) of the per-task ratios, its worst misses, and a sentence: "Work in :backend: takes 1.6× as long as estimated: multiply estimates by 1.6." The multiplier is the median rounded to a tenth, and is only given for three tasks or more.

    A day of EFFORT is 24 hours unless day says otherwise - org's own reading, and what the weekly review and the column view use. Somebody who writes 1d for a working day passes day=8; DayEfforts says how many estimates are written in days, which is when it matters. A week is five days, as common.ParseDuration has it.

    What cannot be measured is counted, not dropped: ClockNoEffort (a task with time on it and no estimate above or below it, with the ten biggest in Unestimated), EffortNoClock (finished with an estimate and no clock) and Rollups (an EFFORT over other estimated headings - a sum, which would count the same work twice). Cancelled tasks are never measured.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    query string no Only the tasks this finds. Default: every heading with a keyword.
    by string no tag (default), project, file or person (ASSIGNEE…).
    block string no A clock table block: thismonth, lastweek, 2026-Q3…
    from string no First day, as typed anywhere (2026-09-01, -90d).
    to string no Last day, inclusive.
    day number no Hours in a day of EFFORT. Default 24.
